results.reason: Issue 1 cites Supply Agreement §14.2. It explains that a change of more than 50% of voting stock is deemed an assignment requiring Vantrell's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It notes that Schedule 4.4 says "None" and that §§6.3 and 7.2(c) do not reach the consent.

Issue 15 cites §16.1. It notes that Corbel cannot assign without consent while Supplier may assign to any Person, including on a sale of its resin business. It flags the risk that Vantrell can transfer the contract to a third party without Corbel's consent. This loosely covers the undesirable-transferee risk, though 'competitor' is not explicit.

Issue 2 computes the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026 and notes it passed before the September 21 SPA date. It states the option cannot be exercised after the deadline and discusses extension pricing.

Issue 3 quotes 'solely Sections 4.1 and 4.2' and explains that §11.11 gives the Side Letter precedence. It states that Capitalization and Taxes lose uncapped treatment and become subject to the Deductible and Cap.

Issue 4 identifies Side Letter §§6.1–6.2 (Delaware law, Chancery) against SPA §§11.8–11.9 (New York). It explains that indemnity claims would be split across forums and laws, and Issue 3 establishes Side Letter precedence.
The response states Cap = 10% of the Purchase Price = $8,450,000.
The response states §11.11 sets an order of precedence with the Side Letter first and the SPA second.
The response is a memorandum to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Fix.
Issues are ordered Critical, then High, Medium, and Clean-up. Part 4 lists the calls with the client before responding.
The response states the deadline passed and the option cannot be exercised after the deadline. It never says the window is open.
The response states the Side Letter controls and that Capitalization and Taxes become subject to the cap. It does not claim the opposite.
